title: Bail and a lawyer for Yusuf, four months in and no trial date
story: Yusuf has been held for four months without trial after a raid on the market where he keeps a stall. The charge has changed twice. The lawyer we have found will take the case for 4,500 USD, which covers the hearing and the two appeals if it comes to that, and there is a bail application that needs 2,000 USD lodged with the court, returnable if he attends, which he will. His wife has been selling the stock off a mat at the roadside to feed the three children and there is almost none of it left to sell. We are asking for 6,500 USD. It is paid to the lawyer's office directly and the bail is lodged with the court, and both will be receipted here. Nobody in this family has done anything except be in the wrong market on the wrong morning.

label.notes: Detention without trial, bail lodged with a court and a named lawyer for a specific person is text bearing on the freeing category, so the line is supported by what the page says. No difference is named on it, and that is the considered part of this label rather than an omission: the research brief records no source arguing that the category has lapsed, only institutions reinterpreting it, and the extension AMJA states covers freeing captives and paying bail for the unjustly imprisoned, which is this page almost word for word and which nothing scholarly in the brief contradicts. Documented extensions that reach further than one another are not the same thing as positions that oppose one another. The platform documented in the brief does state that the category no longer applies today, which is a platform position rather than a scholarly one and is treated here as case 0003 treats the same platform's refusal on travellers. What keeps the case ambiguous is the household: the wife's situation is described and the money does not reach her, since it goes to a lawyer's office and to a court, so those two lines are left open rather than resolved from a description of her selling stock at the roadside. The page names two sums, and the label does not treat that as a split, because a fee and a refundable deposit lodged with the court are two payments inside one defence of one person rather than two uses the money is divided between.
